chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Lunceford's difficult saxophone book
summary: McRae studied "Walking by the River" and its double-time sax chorus, expecting his Chick Webb background to carry him.

I went and got most of his records, I familiarized myself with some of the hard things in his book that he had (inaudible).

"Walking By The River," that was a great thing by Una Mae Carlisle. He had a great arrangement on that.
I think Sol (inaudible) made the arrangement -- I forget who made (inaudible). But I know it was really a tough arrangement especially with the saxophone (inaudible) because it was a double-up chorus.
And they had a little bet on that that I couldn't play the book.
What do you mean a double-up chorus?
You know, like stuff like Benny Carter writes, you know, saxophone, you know. Real fast.

Yeah, like double time.
Like you say (singing notes), you know,

Now here I'm coming out there, you know. They say, let me (inaudible) get Teddy McRae. He'll play it (inaudible). Jimmy say, "Let me get Teddy McRae." I guess they figured that if you come
